firstMismatch.message: Replay error: ARTICLE_YOUR is not defined

mismatch.message: Replay error: ARTICLE_YOUR is not defined

summary: The first mismatch is a JavaScript ReferenceError in mon.c:newcham’s tame old-form naming: js/mon.js:shapeOldNames uses ARTICLE_YOUR but js/mon.js does not import it from js/const.js. C passes ARTICLE_YOUR to do_name.c:x_monnam for a tame monster, and the existing JS x_monnam already supports that article. Importing the existing constant fixes the general source path; this is a divergence fix, not missing C behavior.

source.branch: When NC_SHOW_MSG is set, newcham captures the old tame monster name before changing form by calling x_monnam(mtmp, ARTICLE_YOUR, NULL, SUPPRESS_SADDLE, FALSE); this branch is reached when a mounted tame steed is polymorphed by a trap and is sighted or sensed.

evidence: Saved queue provenance: v39 manifest SHA-256 02e1d34e578b14e273a1916991d10e6ce67e585118338a2c2d45f322b63e81d0; recording SHA-256 1a61a52d42ce5f5596e73f970f91b94ef2b87d33b7740bc2eb6a2735dfb63997; evaluation challenges/evaluations/20261009230658-v39.json from 30d1b7936740e5f611781c85242eb860218d9e5d. The selected case is the highest remaining independent mount/polymorph candidate after C claimed the first case and B claimed the second.

The admitted recipe is independently C-replay byte-identical (manifest v39 sourceTrace cReplay outputSha256 equals the recording hash). Its C result names the tame mount as “Your pony” when a polymorph trap changes the mount; the manifest identifies reported segment 1 step 28 (one-based) as the first JS failure, before steed.c:poly_steed.

Upstream nethack-c/upstream/src/trap.c:steedintrap (around 3154-3156) calls newcham(steed, NULL, NC_SHOW_MSG) for a mounted steed hit by a polymorph trap; trap.c:trapeffect_poly_trap also calls newcham for a non-hero trapped tame monster. Upstream mon.c:newcham (5278-5534; old-name construction around 5308-5315) passes ARTICLE_YOUR for mtmp->mtame and suppresses the saddle. The later call to poly_steed is at mon.c:5518.

The naming callee is defined in do_name.c:x_monnam at 827. It retains ARTICLE_YOUR only for tame monsters and formats it as “your ”; the JS counterpart js/do_name.js imports ARTICLE_YOUR and has the corresponding article branch. The v39 manifest labels this pointer objnam.c, but the actual C definition is in do_name.c.

js/mon.js:shapeOldNames at 2758 references ARTICLE_YOUR without importing it. js/const.js exports ARTICLE_YOUR, while js/mon.js imports ARTICLE_A, ARTICLE_NONE, and ARTICLE_THE only. Fresh-process replay `node frozen/ps_test_runner.mjs --worker-session=challenges/cases/v39/v39-mounted-steed-polymorph-trap.session.json` stopped at moves 28 with error `ARTICLE_YOUR is not defined`; its JSON result is saved in .cache/a2-v39-mounted-steed.before.log (0/29 screens, 0/2642 RNG calls, 0/29 cursors because replay aborts).

Actionable fix: add ARTICLE_YOUR to js/mon.js’s existing const.js import and add a focused source-pinned test in scripts/mon.test.mjs that invokes newcham with NC_SHOW_MSG on a tame monster and verifies its old-name message. The existing x_monnam implementation handles the name; do not change trap behavior, steed logic, naming logic, or session data.
